This incubation duration is relatively compact compared to other members of the family Muscicapidae, likely reflecting the species' adaptation to short, productive summers in its temperate and boreal breeding grounds. Upon hatching, the altricial nestlings exhibit an initial wet body mass averaging 2.24 grams [Ww0 = 2.24 grams]. This modest starting mass, typical of passerines that produce small eggs relative to adult size, necessitates an intensive period of parental provisioning. The newly emerged chicks are entirely dependent on both parents for brooding and food delivery during the first days post-hatching, a critical interval during which they must rapidly acquire somatic tissue to progress through subsequent developmental stages.

A sustained period of parental care and feeding follows the hatching phase, with the next major developmental milestone being the achievement of fledging. Under the standard thermal conditions approximating the birds' active metabolic state during the breeding season, approximately 40.2 °C [T = 40.2 °C], the time since birth at fledging for Larvivora cyane nestlings is 16 days [tx = 16 days] and the time since birth at puberty is 48 days [tp = 48 days]. This rapid transition from nest-bound chick to volant juvenile is characteristic of many small-bodied migratory songbirds, which must achieve independence swiftly to capitalize on peak insect abundance. The nestlings undergo a pronounced phase of feather growth and motor skill development during this fortnight, culminating in their first flight. Sexual maturity, however, is not achieved concurrently with fledging, indicating a considerable post-fledging period required for full gonadal maturation and the acquisition of definitive adult plumage.

Reported clutch sizes for Larvivora cyane range between 4 and 6 eggs per clutch [N_R_i = between 4 and 6 eggs per clutch], a fecundity that is moderate for a ground-nesting insectivore of its body size. The timing of this first reproductive event is closely linked to post-pubertal development. Under the prevailing ambient conditions approximated by an internal body temperature of 40.2 °C [T = 40.2 °C], field records indicate that the time since birth at first brood is 365 days [tR = 365 days]. This interval reveals that the Siberian blue robin defers its initial breeding attempt until the spring following its hatching year, a pattern consistent with other small passerines that require a full season of foraging experience and territory establishment before attempting to reproduce.

Adult body mass in the Siberian blue robin exhibits a modest degree of sexual size dimorphism, a trait commonly observed in monogamous territorial songbirds. The ultimate wet weight for females averages 13.5 grams [Wwi = 13.5 grams], whereas males attain a slightly larger asymptotic mass. Energetic demands during the active breeding period are substantial.
